title: Morgan Stanley Aims for Quarterly Bond Revenue Above $1 Billion
description: Jun.13 -- Morgan Stanley's Chief Executive Officer James Gorman told an industry conference on Tuesday that quarterly bond revenue above $1 billion is a sustainable goal for the firm. Bloomberg's Jason Kelly reports on "Bloomberg Daybreak: Americas."

asr.full_text: The headline yesterday, this is at an investor and industry conference, James Gorman said that Morgan Stanley goal generating about a billion dollars in quarterly average bond trading revenue is too conservative. Right. That's not what we are hearing from other banks. No, it is interesting to see how bullish he is on that specific part of the market. Now keep in mind and we have talked about this at this table a bunch, this year has been pretty good for that part of the business and that desk, in a lot of places, especially at Morgan Stanley. And this is and you guys have both spent some time with James Gorman. This is a sweet spot for them. They've invested pretty heavily and notably in this story, they talk about electronic trading. They invested heavily in equities and now investing even more heavily in bonds it sounds like. Absolutely right. But at the same time having talked to all the people with Morgan Stanley, they also, about two or three years ago, did a consolidation in their trading. They actually let people go and put departments together. And it seems that they're doing so well actually being more streamlined. What I also found so interesting, and I understand that this is not FIC. It's just about bond trading, but a lot of other banks have come out with their FICive sort of forecasts and they don't seem that happy about the second quarter. They say, eh, it's a little bit softer, not as good as the first. This is stark contrast. Well, and this is also and you alluded to this, David. I mean, Gorman has been doing some… … pulling some pretty big levers over at Morgan Stanley, rather quietly. I know you've sat down with him at length fairly recently. This is not a subtle overhaul. This is part of a pretty, a series of pretty major moves that he's making. Exactly right. Presuming, looks like it's starting to pay off. That's a lot of money.
